Rashi on Eruvin 20a:10:1.english: They only taught - That it is called a partition:

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:10:2.hebrew: אלא לזרוק - שהזורק מרה"ר לתוכה חייב, דמדאורייתא ודאי מחיצה היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:10:2.english: Only to throw - That one who throws from the public domain into it is liable, for by Torah law it is certainly a partition:

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:10:3.english: But to carry is forbidden - For the Rabbis decreed against it.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:11:1.hebrew: אמזיד איתמר - וקנסא קנסוה, אבל שוגג מותר. והא דנעשית מאליה — כל שכן דמותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:11:1.english: It was stated regarding [one who acted] intentionally - And [the Sages] imposed a penalty on him; but [if done] unwittingly, [carrying] is permitted. And as for that which was formed on its own, all the more so is it permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:12:1.english: One who throws - From the public domain into [the area] between the upright boards of wells.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:12:2.hebrew: חייב - חטאת, דרשות היחיד מעלייתא הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:12:2.english: Is liable - [To bring] a sin-offering, for it is a full-fledged private domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:12:3.hebrew: אי לאו מחיצה - מדאורייתא היא, לשוויה מיהא רשות היחיד לזריקה:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:12:3.english: Were it not a partition - [Were it not that] it is [a partition] by Torah law, to at least render it a private domain regarding throwing:

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:12:4.hebrew: היכי שרו רבנן למלאות - ולהוציא מרה"י לרה"ר משום דוחק:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:12:4.english: How did the Rabbis permit drawing [water] - and taking [it] out from a private domain to a public domain on account of hardship?

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:13:1.english: Similar to the upright boards surrounding a well - And there is no well there.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:16:1.english: Intersects them - That there is no path there except between the upright boards.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:16:2.english: He must divert it to the sides - For the treading of the public comes and nullifies the partitions.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:16:3.hebrew: כאן הודיעוך - חכמים, כמה גדול כחן של מחיצות, דלא מיבטלי משום בקיעת רבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:16:3.english: Here they informed you - The Sages [informed you] how great is the strength of partitions, that they are not nullified on account of the passage of the public.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:19:1.english: It is permitted to bring [the upright boards] closer, etc. - We explained this entire mishna at the beginning of our chapter.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:19:2.hebrew: אלא א"כ הכניס ראשו ורובו - דחיישינן שמא ימשך גופו למקום רגליו, ויוציא הכלי עמו:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:19:2.english: Unless he brings his head and most of his [body] - For we are concerned lest his body be drawn to the place of his feet, and he bring the vessel out with him.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:2:1.hebrew: אמר ליה מותר - דהא ליכא דיורין בין הפסין דליסרו עלייהו, דליהוי מוציא מרשותו לרשות חבירו:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:2:1.english: He said to him: It is permitted - For there are no residents between the boards who would restrict them, such that he would be carrying out from his domain into his fellow's domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:3:1.hebrew: שתים מאי - שתים זו אצל זו, ומחיצה ביניהן, ושתיהן ראשן בין הפסין:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:3:1.english: Two, what [is the law]? - Two [courtyards] adjacent to each other, with a partition between them, and both have their open end between the [upright] boards.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:3:2.hebrew: אסור - לטלטל מתוכן לבין הפסין, כדמפרש טעמא רב הונא:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:3:2.english: It is prohibited - to carry from inside them to [the area] between the upright boards, as Rav Huna explains the reason.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:4:1.hebrew: ואפילו עירבו - דרך הפתח שבמחיצה שביניהן, דהשתא חדא נינהו ולא אסרן אהדדי — אסורות לטלטל מתוכן לבין הפסין, גזירה שמא יאמרו: עירוב מועיל בין הפסין לשתף חצירות יחד; שהרואה אותן מטלטלין מתוכן לבין הפסין לא ידע דיש פתח ביניהן, וסבר: האי דלא אסרן אהדדי בתוך בין הפסין, כשאר שתי חצירות הפתוחות למבוי אחד — שאסור להוציא למבוי אלא א"כ נשתתפו — ה"נ משום דנתנו עירובן בין הפסין לשתף כשיתוף שאר מבוי, ואתו למשרי נמי להכניס ולהוציא מבין הפסין לחצירות כי ליכא פתח ביניהן ויהבי עירוב באחת החצירות דרך בין הפסין; וההוא ודאי לא מהני, דכי תקינו רבנן שיתופי מבואות — במבוי סתום תקון, ואורכו יותר על רחבו, וזה מפולש לארבעה צדדין:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:4:1.english: And even if they made an eiruv - Via the doorway that is in the partition between them, so that now they are [considered] one [courtyard] and do not prohibit one another — they are [nevertheless] prohibited to carry from within them to [the area] between the boards, as a decree lest [people] say: An eiruv is effective between the boards to join courtyards together. For one who sees them carrying from within them to [the area] between the boards will not know that there is a doorway between them, and will think: Just as with any other two courtyards opening into one alleyway, where it is prohibited to carry out into the alleyway unless they joined in a shituf, this [fact] that they do not prohibit one another within [the area] between the boards is likewise because they placed their eiruv between the boards to join together, like the shituf of other alleyways; and they will come to also permit bringing [items] in and taking [them] out between [the area] between the boards and the courtyards when there is no doorway between them, and they place an eiruv in one of the courtyards via [the area] between the boards. And that certainly is not effective, for when the Sages instituted the shituf of alleyways, they instituted [it] for a closed alleyway whose length exceeds its width, whereas this [enclosure] is open on all four sides.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:5:1.hebrew: עירבו מותרין - דכיון דעירבו דרך פתח שביניהן, וחד רשותא הוא דלא אסרן אהדדי — להך גזירה לא חיישינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:5:1.english: [If] they made an eiruv, they are permitted - For since they made an eiruv via the opening between them, and it is a single domain so that they do not prohibit one another — we are not concerned about that decree.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:6:1.hebrew: דהדרן וערבן - שנפרצה ביניהן פירצה גדולה בסופה, שגלוי לכל שרשות אחת היא: (*):(*)
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:6:1.english: Where they later became joined - That a large breach opened between them at its end, so that it is evident to all that it is a single domain. (*):(*)

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:7:1.hebrew: יבשו מים בשבת מהו - לטלטל בין הפסין: מי אמרינן: שבת, הואיל והותרה — הותרה; או דילמא, כיון דהיתר פסין אינו אלא משום מים, והרי יבשו — ואסור? ואכל פסי ביראות קאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:7:1.english: If the water dried up on Shabbat, what is [the law] - [With regard to] carrying between the [upright] boards: Do we say, [with regard to] Shabbat, since it was permitted [at its onset], it remains permitted [for the entire day]; or perhaps, since the allowance of the [upright] boards is only on account of the water, and behold, it dried up, it is forbidden? And [this question] refers to all partitions around cisterns.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:7:2.hebrew: כלום נעשית מחיצה - כלומר, כלום הותרה מחיצה כזו אלא משום מים:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:7:2.english: Was a partition made at all - That is to say, was such a partition permitted at all except on account of [the] water?

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:8:1.hebrew: יבשו מים בשבת - וחזרו ובאו גשמים בו ביום, מאי? מי אמרינן: חזרו פסין להיתרן הראשון לטלטל בתוכן:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:8:1.english: [If] water dried up on Shabbat - And rain returned and came on that same day, what [is the law]? Do we say [that] the [upright] boards return to their initial permitted status to carry within them?

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:8:2.english: Of the Master - Rabbah, who was his teacher.

Rashi on Eruvin 20a:9:1.hebrew: ובאו מים בשבת לא קמבעיא לי - דמותר, דהא קיימא לן: כל מחיצה הנעשית בשבת שמה מחיצה:
Rashi on Eruvin 20a:9:1.english: And [that] water came on Shabbat is not a dilemma for me - That it is permitted, for we maintain: Any partition made on Shabbat is considered a partition.

Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:11:1.hebrew: כי איתמר דרב נחמן אמזיד איתמר - והא דאמרינן בשבת בפרק הזורק (שבת ד' קא:): "ספינות שנתקשרו מערב שבת והותרו וחזרו ונתקשרו, בין שוגגין ובין מזידין ובין מוטעין ובין אנוסין — חזרו להיתרן הראשון" — במזיד, לא חזרו לגמרי להיתרן הראשון לטלטל, אלא דהוו רשות היחיד דאורייתא. אי נמי: לא קאי אמזיד:
Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:11:1.english: "When Rav Naḥman’s statement was stated, it was stated regarding [one who erected it] intentionally" - And as for that which we say in Shabbat in the chapter [entitled] HaZorek (Shabbat 101b): "[With regard to] boats that were tied together from Shabbat eve, and were untied, and were tied together again — whether unwittingly, or intentionally, or mistakenly, or under duress — they have returned to their initial permitted status" — [in the case of one who acted] intentionally, they did not completely return to their initial permitted status [such that it would be permitted] to carry, but rather [it means only] that they are a private domain by Torah law. Alternatively, [the statement "they have returned to their initial permitted status"] does not apply to [the case of one who acted] intentionally.

Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:17:1.hebrew: קמ"ל כאן וסבירא ליה - ומיהו לר' יוחנן, ודאי "כאן" — ולא ס"ל, כדאמרי' לקמן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:17:1.english: "He teaches us 'here' and he agrees" - However, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, [what he meant was] certainly "here," but he does not agree [with them], as we say later.

Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:19:1.hebrew: לא יעמוד אדם - בפרק בתרא (ד' צט.) מוקי לה בחפצים הצריכין לו, וגזרי' דלמא יכניס אצלו. וקשיא: דתיפוק ליה דקא מעייל מרשות הרבים לרשות היחיד, כמו משתין ורק מרשות הרבים לרה"י דאסרינן לקמן! ורש"י תירץ לקמן: דלא דמי למשתין ורק, דשותה עביד עקירה והנחה בחד רשותא, דמשקין נחין בתוך פיו שהוא מקום פטור, ואע"ג דחוזרין ונבלעין — אין לחוש, הואיל ונחו במקום פטור. ואע"ג דבמקום שאין בו ד' על ד' (אמות) אמרינן "ובלבד שלא יחליפו", התם גזרינן דילמא אתי לאפוקי בהדיא, אבל הכא אי אפשר כלל שלא ינוחו מעט בפיו קודם שיבלעם. אבל במשתין ורק, לא חשיב פיו מקום פטור, כיון דפיו וגופו הן במקום א'. ולפי זה, היה מותר להוציא ראשו מרה"ר ולרוק, כיון דפיו במקום אחר הוי מקום פטור. והא דמבעיא לן בפרק בתרא (ד' צט.) "הוא ברה"י ופי האמה ברה"ר מהו" — היינו משום דמי רגלים, מיד כשנעקרו מגופו, שוב אין נחים בפי האמה. אבל מפ"ק דשבת (ד' ג:) קשיא, דקאמרינן התם: "אדרבה, משחשיכה, דאי שדי ליה אתי לידי חיוב חטאת, לא קנסינן", והשתא היכי אתי לידי חיוב חטאת? הואיל ונחו בידו, שהוא מקום פטור! וי"ל: דלא חשיב הנחה במקום פטור אלא בדבר שהוא נוטל ממקומו, אבל התם, שהכלי נח מאליו, לא חשיב הנחה במקום פטור; ולפי זה, אסור להוציא ראשו ברה"ר ולרוק. וא"ת: אכתי אפשר דלא אתי לידי חיוב חטאת, כגון שיתן מידו זאת לידו אחרת? וי"ל: דאיירי כשהנקב קטן, שלא יוכל להכניס בו שתי ידיו. ועוד נראה לפרש: דלא דמי למשתין ורק, דהכא כשבולעם, מיד חשיבי כנחין, אע"ג דאינם נחים עד שיגיעו למעיו, משום דמבטלי אגב גופו, והוי עקירה והנחה בחד רשותא. והכי נמי אמר רבא בפ' המוציא (שבת ד' פ.): הוציא שתי אותיות וכתבן כשהוא מהלך — חייב, דכתיבתן זו היא הנחתן. ואתי נמי שפיר מתניתין ד"אמרו לו", גבי "יש אוכל אכילה אחת כו' ר' מאיר אומר: אם היה שבת והוציא בפיו — חייב". והשתא, היכי חשיב הוצאה בהדי הנך? הא בעידנא דמיחייב עלייהו, דהיינו בשעת הנחת גרון, אכתי לא מיחייב אהוצאה עד שינוחו במעיו! אלא, אהוצאה נמי מחייב משעת בליעה, דחשיב כמונח:
Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:19:1.english: A person may not stand - In the last chapter (99a), [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring] to objects that he needs, and we decree lest he bring [them] in to himself. And [this is] difficult: Let him derive [the prohibition from the fact] that he is bringing [the water] in from the public domain to the private domain, just like urinating and spitting from the public domain into the private domain, which we prohibit later (99b)! And Rashi answered later: It is not comparable to urinating and spitting, for one who drinks performs the uprooting and the placing in a single domain, as the liquids come to rest inside his mouth, which is an exempt domain; and even though they are subsequently swallowed, there is no concern [of a Torah violation], since they rested in an exempt domain. And even though regarding a place that does not have four by four [cubits] we say, "provided that they do not exchange [directly]," there we decree lest he come to carry it out directly, whereas here it is entirely impossible that they should not rest slightly in his mouth before he swallows them. However, in [the case of] one who urinates or spits, his mouth is not considered an exempt domain, since his mouth and his body are in one place. And according to this, it would be permitted [for one standing in the public domain] to extend his head from the public domain and spit, since his mouth in another place constitutes an exempt domain. And as for that which was asked to us in the last chapter (99b): "If he is in the private domain and the tip of the penis is in the public domain, what is [the ruling]?" — that is because urine, immediately once uprooted from his body, no longer rests at the tip of the penis. However, from the first chapter of Shabbat (3b) it is difficult, for we say there: "On the contrary, [if he stuck bread in the oven on Friday] after it became dark, where if he drops it he will incur liability for a sin-offering, we do not penalize [him]"; and now, how could he incur liability for a sin-offering, since [the loaves] rested in his hand, which is an exempt domain?! And it can be answered: It is not considered a placement in an exempt domain except with regard to an object that one takes from its place; but there, where the vessel [or bread] comes to rest on its own, it is not considered a placement in an exempt domain. And according to this, it is forbidden to extend one's head into the public domain and spit. And if you say: Still, it is possible that he would not incur liability for a sin-offering, such as if he transfers [the bread] from this hand of his to his other hand? And it can be answered: It is dealing with [a case] where the aperture is small, such that he cannot insert both of his hands into it. And furthermore, it seems [preferable] to explain: that it is not comparable to urinating and spitting, because here, when he swallows them, they are immediately considered as having come to rest — even though they do not actually rest until they reach his stomach — because they become nullified to his body, and it is [thus] an uprooting and a placing in a single domain. And so too said Rava in the chapter [entitled] HaMotzi (Shabbat 80a): "If one carried out two letters and wrote them while walking, he is liable, for writing them is their placing." And the Mishnah in [the chapter entitled] "Amru Lo" [Keritot 13b] also works out well, regarding: "There is [a case of] one who eats a single eating... Rabbi Meir says: If it was Shabbat and he carried [the food] out in his mouth, he is liable." And now, how can [the Mishnah] count carrying out [on Shabbat] together with those [other transgressions]? For at the time when he becomes liable for those — namely, at the moment of swallowing down the throat — he would not yet be liable for carrying out until [the food] rests in his stomach! Rather, for carrying out he also becomes liable from the moment of swallowing, as it is considered as having come to rest.

Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:6:1.hebrew: דהדרן וערבן - והכי פירושו: שתים אסורות — אפי' עירבו; ו"אם עירבו" כו' — דהיינו כלומר: דהדרן וערבן, מותרות כשעירבו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:6:1.english: Where they later became joined - And this is its explanation: "Two are forbidden" — even if they made an eiruv; and "if they made an eiruv, etc." — that is to say: [in a case] where they later became joined, they are permitted when they made an eiruv.

Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:7:1.hebrew: מחיצה אין כאן - אע"ג דאביי אית ליה "שבת, הואיל והותרה — הותרה", מודה הכא, משום דליכא מחיצות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 20a:7:1.english: There is no partition here - Even though Abaye maintains [the principle that with regard to] Shabbat, since it was permitted, it remains permitted, he concedes here, because there are no partitions.
